title: Normalize the test function in the quantitative pairing bound
reason: The chapter gives the square root of the product of the local bounds for a bounded frame-invariant test function. Lean assumes a measurable function of modulus at most 1 and requires its product with the cut kernel to vanish outside the frame boxes. The integral and the cut error scale with the test function. For a general bounded test, its supremum norm also multiplies the square-root term.
proposed_correction: State the unit bound and support condition. For the displayed radii ρᵥ, require ρᵥ ≥ b^(6n+2) and a common y′ with y′ᵥ and γᵥ⁻¹y′ᵥ in the radius-ρᵥ box at each place. The quantity bounded is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the integral.

title: Use the global size parameter for the stationary-point entry bound
reason: The substitution sets a = ccᵥ(1) and then L = 3a. The stationary-point theorem needs L to bound every entry of both Harish-Chandra parameters. Lean supplies these bounds with L = 3·D.a (FillingData.lean lines 235–236, 350 and 375). At places outside D.aPlaces the local column count is zero by Weights.lean lines 53–55. Then the proposed L is zero, which is incompatible with the large-gap parameter on the indefinite group.
proposed_correction: Write aᵥ = ccᵥ(1) for the distinguished lowest K-type weight and L = 3·D.a for the common bound. Keep 3·D.a as the bound in steps 2 and 6.

title: The proof applies the fixer-measure density twice
reason: The linked definition uses μ_d = c_G d^(k−1) dh du. Step 3 sets c = c_G (g(Z)/2)^(k−1) and then uses μ_c, which has density c_G c^(k−1). Step 5 instead uses mass c · vol(Ω₀). Conditioning cancels a constant in m, but ν also contains the inverse of this mass, so the claimed bound for the proposed ν does not follow.
proposed_correction: Set d = g(Z)/2 and c = c_G d^(k−1). Take μ = μ_d = c · dh du throughout. This gives the step-5 mass and the Sobolev measure used in step 4.

title: The second moment sums squared absolute values of Petersson products
reason: The chapter describes the second moment as a sum of Petersson products. In Lean it is the sum over s of ‖P* s P‖²_HS. In coordinates this sums the squared moduli of the pairings. The pairings themselves may be complex and cancel, so summing them would not give this nonnegative moment.
proposed_correction: Say that each pairing unfolds to a block entry and that the second moment sums the squared absolute values of those entries, with the scale of the chosen P.

title: Theorem B bounds the dimension of the span
reason: Theorem B gives a finite collection of translates of the normalized map on ramified source forms whose images span at least (1−4/b²) times the target dimension. Its conclusion permits a complement of positive dimension. Saying the translates fill the space states a stronger result.
proposed_correction: Give the proportion 1−4/b², or say that the chosen translates span all but a proportion at most 4/b² of the target.

title: Bound frame vectors on each Bessel-length layer
reason: A nonzero class cutoff gives the box bound at scale R when the local Bessel length is at most b^(6n+2)R. Its entire support has no uniform frame bound. The unipotent action fixes the first frame vector, so a split diagonal dilation can make ‖y⁻¹e₁‖ arbitrarily large on a whole orbit. The cutoff partition of unity still gives a nonzero value somewhere on that orbit.
proposed_correction: Say that on the local Bessel-length layer ℓ(yᵥ) ≤ b^(6n+2)R the support lies in the frame box of radius b^(37n)R.

title: The Poincaré series have uniformly bounded absolute sums
reason: Lean proves that ∑γ |Bₐ(γg)| is bounded by a constant independent of g. This gives absolute convergence at each g. Uniform convergence of the partial sums on the whole adelic group would force the individual summands to tend uniformly to zero. For a nonzero seed, every translate has the same positive supremum norm as Bₐ, which rules this out for infinite Γ.
proposed_correction: Replace “converge uniformly” with “converge absolutely at every g, with the absolute sums bounded uniformly in g”.

title: Normalize the generic character before identifying the Bessel period
reason: For a general fitting space, the Bessel character restricts to the generic unipotent character under the additional condition ȷ c_Y = −(Mϖ)⁻¹. The grading permits other choices of the nonzero real scalar c_Y with the same underlying groups. The period identity in SeriesPeriod.lean:620 needs the same condition. The data D satisfy it separately at lines 699–704.
proposed_correction: State the normalization of the Weil scalar and generic constant in Section 8. Point out that the grading of D satisfies it in Section 9.

title: The displayed levels identify the last hyperbolic pair with the middle block
reason: The page numbers e₁ through eϱ and assigns eϱ, eϱ* and the middle block the same level ϱ. Its block-unitriangular condition then excludes I+iE_{eϱ,eϱ*}, an isometry of the last hyperbolic plane that belongs to Lean’s unipotent group. The case split in the proof also uses the strict separation of these levels.
proposed_correction: Use e₀,…,e_{ϱ−1} throughout with the stated levels, or keep one-based labels and give eₐ and eₐ* levels a−1 and 2ϱ−a+1.

title: A uniform bound for the absolute sums does not give uniform convergence on G
reason: The theorem proves pointwise absolute convergence with one bound C for all g. Its terms do not tend uniformly to zero on the full adelic group. If Bₐ(g₀) is nonzero, every translate takes this same value at g = γ⁻¹g₀. Such a point exists by orthonormality of the full Bessel coordinates and their recovery from the class-unipotent sum. The rational subgroup contains infinitely many scalar elements of norm one.
proposed_correction: Retitle the page “Uniform bound for the absolute Poincaré sums and integrability of the cut-off Bessel functions”. Keep the two numbered claims as written.

title: Separate the last isotropic, middle and first dual levels
reason: The page numbers e₁ through eρ starting at 1, then uses Lean’s zero-based formula. It assigns eρ, the entire middle block and eρ* the same level ρ. Take x=eρ, u=0 and a nonzero integral skew scalar s in the page’s own construction. The resulting γ has entry Ms at (eρ,eρ*), which the stated equal-level rule forbids. This example works at every rank allowed by the filling data.
proposed_correction: With 1≤a≤ρ use levels a−1, ρ and 2ρ−a+1 for eₐ, the middle block and eₐ* respectively. These put the two sides of each hyperbolic plane strictly across the middle.

title: Group the summands with the unipotent factor on the left
reason: The displayed group sums have arguments q̃u g. The cutoff identity used in the next sentence sums Bₐ(uδg), so it cannot collapse the displayed sum unless extra normalization by q̃ is proved. Lean indexes by q in G_S(E)/U but its bijection sends (q,u) to u q.out⁻¹. The kernel-fixing step at PoincareSeries.lean lines 529–532 uses δ = ρ(q.out⁻¹).
proposed_correction: For each representative q̃ take the right coset U q̃⁻¹ and set F_q(g) = ∑ᵤ Bₐ(ρ(u q̃⁻¹)g). Property 3 now applies at δg with δ = ρ(q̃⁻¹).

title: Include the formal degree and the square in the period identity
reason: The period at x is ⟨v,W(x)⟩ = deg(λ)·‖W‖₂² for the unnormalized average of a unit vector v. Calling the period its L² norm loses both the square and the formal degree. The stationary-point step uses the size of this period compared with the volume of the unit ball in the period group.
proposed_correction: Give the identity for the unnormalized average before describing its normalization. Mention that the quantitative lower bound comes from the steep parameter and matching compact type in the linked stationary-point theorem.

title: Specify that rep is a continuous unitary representation
reason: The displayed input is a continuous map into a unitary group. The proof of equivariance uses its multiplication and inverse laws to factor the operator π(s) out of the translated integral. Continuity and unitary values alone do not supply those laws.
proposed_correction: Introduce rep as a continuous group homomorphism U(κ) → U(I), as required in the linked definition of the Bessel average.

title: Include the degree hypothesis in the local-bounds application
reason: The quoted local-bounds theorem has a separate hypothesis 4000n ≤ f. The listed RealPlaceSizes controls the box radius, ranks, exponent and base, and has no f parameter. FillingData.lean lines 407–409 supplies this final inequality from admissibility.
proposed_correction: Add 4000n ≤ f to step 7 and cite the data’s size estimates. The volume-of-balls premise in the same sentence is for T ≥ 1.

title: Use the radial majorant in the volume-of-balls argument
reason: The outline attributes the ball-volume estimate to Chebyshev applied to the coefficient tail. An upper bound on a coefficient permits it to vanish on the ball. The source integrates the positive radial function φ(g) = deg·(2/‖g‖)ᵐ, with m = 9r², whose lower bound on the ball controls its volume.
proposed_correction: Cite the integral bound for φ and integrate deg ≤ (T/2)ᵐφ(g) over ‖g‖ ≤ T for T ≥ 1.

title: Distinguish the library tail estimate from its specialization in b
reason: The number called the “exact form” of integral_tail_le contains b. The library theorem uses 8·(2000·(r+L+1)⁶)^(2r²)·2ᴹ and has no b parameter. CutTailBound.lean lines 69–78 replaces 8 and 2000 by b and r+L+1 by b⁴. The resulting estimate used in the integral is valid.
proposed_correction: Give the library constant and then state the substitutions using b ≥ 2000 and r+L+1 ≤ b⁴.

title: The displayed mass bound can divide by zero outside the open cell
reason: The page defines the predicate for arbitrary γ and divides by g(Z(γ)). For example, at ϱ = 0 and γ = 1 the frame Gram matrix is [−1] and the discriminant is zero. Lean uses total real division, making pairingBoundSq zero there. The existence theorem separately assumes positive discriminant.
proposed_correction: Give the explicit fraction on the open cell and state how pairingBoundSq is defined when the discriminant vanishes, or state the source convention 0⁻¹ = 0.

title: The intermediate kernel bound carries fewer conditions on the shifts
reason: IsKernelBound does more than replace γt by an arbitrary g and change the radius and mass bound. It imposes neither measurability of t nor frame fixing. Lines 719–721 of the source add those conditions explicitly to pass from the kernel bound to the open-cell bound.
proposed_correction: State that the compactness, probability, contraction, mass and capture fields are retained. List measurability of t and its values in the frame fixer as extra requirements of IsOpenCellBound.

title: Limit the fixed-constant Schur estimate to the stated derivative orders
reason: The summary attributes Schur’s L² bound to derivatives of all orders. The chain rule does hold for every word, but the uniform estimate B^(2s)D in the theorem requires s ≤ 2n². The unrestricted estimate for X_w uses a base growing with the word length. The body gives the correct cutoff at line 27.
proposed_correction: State that right derivatives exist at every order and that the displayed Schur constants apply through order 2n².

title: Subtract the identity in the flag-lowering assertion
reason: Writing A = p⁻¹x⁻¹gxp, it is A−I that sends the first j vectors into the span of the first j−1. A itself preserves their flag. At the identity, A cannot send the nonzero first vector to zero. Similarly g−I induces h−I on the definite coordinates modulo the isotropic span.
proposed_correction: State the flag condition for A−I in the sign frame. State either that A acts by h modulo the preceding vectors, or that A−I acts by h−I there.

title: Use the period estimate for a stationary position
reason: The cited IsPosition.period_lower_bound_of_surjective does not exist. The appendix requires IsStationary, including i₀† μ i₀ = μ′ and the identity on the common X-coordinates. The Gram and flag properties listed in the outline do not provide those two identities. Step 1 actually obtains them from IsSteep.exists_isStationary.
proposed_correction: Cite New.DiscreteSeries.IsStationary.period_lower_bound_of_surjective and carry the two defining identities of its stationary-position input forward from step 1.

title: State the field and admissibility hypotheses used in the unfolding steps
reason: The setting begins with filling data over a CM field. The partition of unity and the analytic block estimates assume that E contains a primitive 5040th root of unity and that S is admissible. The latter has structural conditions beyond the inequalities mentioned on line 30: reduction is onto and the source level is the inverse image of K(M), as specified in Setup.lean:501–505.
proposed_correction: State these standing assumptions once for the results that use them, then explain that Section 9 supplies admissibility for the data D.

title: Moving a block requires the translating pair to preserve the term set
reason: Stability of T is invariance under left and right unipotent multiplication. For rational elements σ,σ′ of the larger Bessel subgroup, the transport lemma separately requires γ∈T exactly when σγσ′⁻¹∈T and requires a continuous linear map implementing the kernel transformation. Arbitrary Bessel translations can change the term set.
proposed_correction: Qualify the first consequence with preservation of T by the translating pair and the corresponding linear transformation of the kernel.

title: Fitting the data also constrains the type, point and grading
reason: The chapter defines a fit by identifying the groups. The group identifications are consequences of a fit. The definition also asks for the local discrete-series Bessel types, the standard grading indices, an idempotent type kernel, the prescribed finite-point congruence and a central η. The same groups may be paired with incompatible types.
proposed_correction: Describe the fit as compatibility of the local types, grading and adelic point with the filling data, and present the group identifications as a consequence.

title: Keep the Weyl-vector factor in the formula for the Bessel function
reason: The tensor product is vector-valued. For each test vector ζ, Lean expresses its scalar pairing with ζ as an integral with three factors: the conjugate type kernel, the inverse Bessel character, and t(a·ζ) for the Levi part a and a chosen linear functional t. Integrating the two scalar character and kernel factors alone loses the dependence on ζ.
proposed_correction: Say that after pairing the tensor product with ζ, one integrates the conjugate type kernel times χ_R(s)⁻¹ t(a·ζ) at a suitable real base point.

title: Restrict the character in the summary to the Bessel group
reason: Lean defines the formula on the full adelic group G but proves multiplicativity for r and r′ in R(𝔸). The simple-root sum is additive on that subgroup. For example, multiplying an arbitrary matrix g by the central −I negates its simple-root sum, although χ(−I)=1. This reverses any nonreal value of χ(g).
proposed_correction: Describe the function on G and identify its restriction to R(𝔸) as the Bessel character.

title: State the Weil scalar in the generic-character identity
reason: The remark leaves “matched” unspecified. The hypothesis is ȷ c_Y = −(Mϖ)⁻¹, where c_Y is fixed by conjugation and ȷ is the purely imaginary element of the Weil data. Equating c_Y alone with the right side would lose this factor. The newly translated SeriesPeriod theorem proves the extension under the displayed condition.
proposed_correction: Give the equality with ȷ and link to the companion knowl bessel-character-extends-generic-character.

title: Restrict conjugation into the principal level to the indicated Levi subgroup
reason: The proof says the finite unipotent character is trivial on elements conjugate into K(M). The cited lemma permits conjugation by the image of the finite unitary group H, which preserves the simple-root character. Conjugation by an arbitrary ambient torus element can rescale a simple-root coordinate.
proposed_correction: Say that ι(η)⁻¹ v ι(η) belongs to K(M) for v = α(u)_f. Apply the cited lemma with its first argument equal to 1 and its Levi variable equal to η to obtain χ(v) = 1.

title: State the field hypothesis for the cutoff partition
reason: Item 4 assumes admissibility of S over a CM field. The cited partition also assumes E contains a primitive 5040th root of unity. The specialization at SeriesPeriod.lean 222 obtains this separate hypothesis from fixed Weil data, and the definition of admissibility supplies only level, reduction, and size conditions.
proposed_correction: Add the primitive 5040th-root hypothesis to item 4, or place this property in the setting of a CM field with the fixed Weil data of SeriesPeriod.lean.

title: Lift the coordinates of the covector before extending it linearly
reason: The text calls m a linear form on the residue space, then sets the integral linear form to ℓ composed with m. The section ℓ is a set map. For nonzero m this composite on the residue space cannot even be additive into the torsion-free integral adeles. Lean applies ℓ to each entry of the row m, and separately to each entry of the row m g.
proposed_correction: On each lattice basis vector eᵢ prescribe the values ℓ(m(eᵢ)) and ℓ(m(g eᵢ)), respectively. Extend these rows linearly over the integral adeles.

title: Identify the prescribed rows as rows of γ−1
reason: The summary says that the row of the group element γ itself is Mℓ. Its diagonal entry is actually 1, whereas ℓ vanishes there. Already for ℓ=s=0 the stated rows of γ agree with the identity. The displayed theorem adds the Kronecker delta correctly.
proposed_correction: Say that γ−1 has row Mℓ at eₐ and zero rows at the other isotropic vectors outside the exceptional column.

title: Sum the contributions when p repeats an index
reason: The lemma allows an arbitrary map p. Row eₐ of xu*J is the sum of rows b of u*J over all b with p(b)=a. The proof identifies that row with a single summand. The same multiplicity occurs when multiplying on the right by x*J. With two equal p-values and equal nonzero contributions, the entry is twice the single contribution.
proposed_correction: Write each matrix product as a sum over the fibre of p and apply the stated vanishing hypothesis to every summand.

title: Include the scalar and skew conditions in the summary
reason: The short statement claims preservation of J under the conditions on x and u alone. With the standard hyperbolic J, x=e₁, u=0, s=g=1 and τ=1/2, the resulting matrix sends e₂ to e₂+e₁, changing its norm from 0 to 2. The detailed statement imposes the missing condition on s.
proposed_correction: State that J is Hermitian, s is skew-Hermitian and g=τ+τ̄, along with the orthogonality assumptions on x and u.

title: Use the same frame indices in the proof and statement
reason: Line 15 defines (f₀,…,fρ)=(e₁,…,eρ,z), so fₐ=eₐ₊₁ for 0≤a<ρ. The proof sets fₐ=eₐ and later takes a∈{1,…,ρ}, which omits the first allowable row and makes e₀ undefined when a=0.
proposed_correction: Use one-based frame indices f₁,…,fρ₊₁ throughout, or retain f₀,…,fρ and consistently replace the associated e-index and row conditions by a+1.

title: The imaginary-coordinate lattice requires the additivity hypothesis
reason: Item (iii) correctly restricts membership to elements for which right multiplication adds the chosen entry. The summary claims it for all elements. On two hyperbolic pairs take A=I+ME₁₂ and a skew matrix H with H₂₁=Mζ, H₁₂=−Mζ̄ for a primitive cube root ζ. The product of diag(A,A^{−*}) with the upper block shear of parameter H is a level-M unipotent and has (e₁,e₁*) entry M²ζ. Its scaled imaginary part would require the skew integer M(ζ−ζ̄)/2, whose norm in ℚ(ζ) is 3M²/4. The level M is odd.
proposed_correction: Say that every skew-lattice value is attained and that membership is proved for elements translating that coordinate additively, in particular after the required earlier coordinates vanish.

title: Include the two determinant hypotheses in the summary
reason: The summary asserts the bound for two integral vectors. Lean requires all earlier rows of the product matrix to vanish and the terminal determinant to be a unit in the finite adeles. The first condition is what allows the kernel relation to descend to two columns. With two zero test vectors the determinant is zero and its generalized index is zero, even though every meet norm is at least one.
proposed_correction: Qualify the summary with the preceding-row vanishing condition and the assumption that the final two-by-two determinant is a finite idele.

title: Distinguish the coordinate pairing from the unitary form
reason: The prose calls the entries h-pairings. The displayed formula and Lean both use the ordinary coordinate conjugate transpose of F = (f | kf), giving Fᴴt. The actual unitary pairing is FᴴJt with the lattice Gram matrix J. For an isotropic frame vector e, its coordinate self-pairing is 1 while h(e,e) is 0.
proposed_correction: Describe Fᴴt as the matrix of standard coordinate pairings. To present a statement with the unitary form, explicitly replace the test matrix by Jt and use unimodularity.

title: Reduce the global conjugate transpose before multiplying
reason: Writing the multiplier as the adjoint of the reduced t uses the wrong residue component. At a split level place p, reduction of tᴴ is the transpose of t reduced at the conjugate place. A place idempotent already distinguishes the two operations. Lean sets T = tᴴ over the integral adeles and reduces T entrywise.
proposed_correction: Write redₚ(tᴴ)(f x − redₚ(k) f y) = 0. Equivalently, its first factor is red at the opposite sign of t, transposed.

title: Include the preservation of the summation set in the summary
reason: The summary says that the hypotheses on the two Bessel elements and on L suffice to carry one block to the other. Blocks sum only over T. The source requires γ in T if and only if σγσ′⁻¹ is in T as a separate condition, even when T is stable under the unipotent groups. Without it the change of variables can relate different summation sets. The main statement includes it.
proposed_correction: Begin the summary with a stable set T preserved by γ ↦ σγσ′⁻¹.

title: State the hypotheses for measurability of the cutoff
reason: The page restricts the standing hypotheses to item 3, leaving measurability in item 2 unconditional. The cited measurability lemma uses admissibility and the primitive-root hypothesis through the class cutoff. Its reduced indicator uses a chosen residue domain, whose existence is proved for admissible data.
proposed_correction: Apply the stated assumptions also to the measurability clause of item 2. Keep the norm bound and right level invariance unconditional. Refer to the convergence proposition for the hypotheses guaranteeing that the displayed Poincaré sum converges absolutely.

title: Keep the level and mass errors in the logarithmic estimate
reason: The outline describes the remainder as linear in log b and the other listed quantities. The range for log N contributes fk√(log b). Lean explicitly reserves that term in the final error estimate. It also uses the finer summed mass error log(1+b⁻⁹)−4f/N to absorb the loss from replacing Nᵏ−1 by Nᵏ.
proposed_correction: State the level error fk√(log b) and the sharper mass error from the linked remark. Distinguish those errors from the linear calculation of the main term and keep the final appeal to the size estimate.

title: Give the integral convention for arbitrary test functions
reason: Item 3 asserts the equality for every function. The Lean statement quantifies over complex-valued functions using the totalized Bochner integral. For example, the constant 1 on this noncompact group with a real unipotent factor has no finite complex Haar integral, although the two Haar measures are proportional.
proposed_correction: State the identity for Haar-integrable complex functions, or retain all functions and specify that the Bochner integral is zero for a nonintegrable test.

title: Qualify the source-level index in the summary
reason: The product description of H̄ holds for every filling. The separate index formula for the source level requires admissibility, which identifies that level with the preimage of K(M). The ambient group in the index is the preimage of the lattice stabilizer in H(𝔸_f). Item 3 of the body states both qualifications.
proposed_correction: State that for admissible data the order of H̄ is the index of the source level in ι⁻¹(K).

title: State the coset normalization in the partition-of-unity summary
reason: The summary says the translates over the entire unipotent congruence subgroup sum to one. For fixed y the indicator is one on a whole right coset of the frame fixer, so the unweighted sum counts the elements of that fixer. The source instead assumes the weight has mass one on each right coset, exactly as in item 4.
proposed_correction: Say that the indicators sum to one over representatives for the right cosets, or that their weighted sum is one for weights normalized on every such coset.

title: Use one indexing convention for the hyperbolic levels
reason: The area chapter labels the vectors e₁,…,eρ. The displayed levels a and 2ρ−a use Lean’s a ∈ Fin ρ, starting at zero. With the chapter labels the formula puts eρ and z at the same level and incorrectly forces the free entry in row eρ, column z to vanish.
proposed_correction: For 1 ≤ a ≤ ρ give eₐ level a−1 and eₐ* level 2ρ−a+1. Alternatively, explicitly relabel the vectors e₀,…,eρ₋₁ before using the current levels.

title: The scale quotient is off by a power of κ for the stated row labels
reason: Step 3 indexes eₐ from 1 to ϱ, while f_b is zero-based. Its stated denominator |κᵥ|^(ϱ−a) is the zero-based one. For a=ϱ and f_b=z the quotient should be 1/|κᵥ|, whereas the displayed equality gives 1. The coarse lower bound used by the rigidity argument still holds.
proposed_correction: Use |κᵥ|^(ϱ−a+1) for a one-based eₐ, or reindex that induction from 0 through ϱ−1. Give the frame column a different letter from the size parameter b.

title: Specify the coefficient of the grading
reason: The setup describes Y through the length of its string and the κ-block. Lean takes a grading with coefficient S.N, the integer N of these filling data. The Gram comparison in lines 111–115 uses the grading’s Gram identity, including the central string vector’s norm −N. The standard labelling alone fixes only the positions of the blocks.
proposed_correction: Specify that Y is a grading of V with coefficient S.N, in which the middle string vector has norm −S.N.

title: Keep the lower bound on u in the layer bound summary
reason: The summary only bounds the mass of sublevels with R ≥ 1. On one point take w = K = e = d = 1, u = 1/4 and i = 3. Every displayed sublevel bound in the summary holds, yet the weighted sum is 64 and the claimed upper bound is 2. The body supplies u ≥ 1.
proposed_correction: Add “for u ≥ 1” to the summary before the sublevel bound.

title: Qualify the twist criterion for ordinary integrals
reason: The last sentence asserts vanishing of the quotient integral of any continuous invariant function with a nontrivial unitary twist. For Γ trivial in the additive real line, F(y)=exp(iy) changes sign under translation by π, but its ordinary Lebesgue integral does not exist. The source uses Lean’s Bochner integral, which takes value zero on nonintegrable functions.
proposed_correction: State the ordinary criterion for functions integrable on the quotient, or specify Lean’s integral convention. For the actual weighted block terms, integrability is part (b) of the cited change-of-weight theorem.

title: Give the squared norm and its formal-degree factor in the summary
reason: The period equals the formal degree times the square of the L² norm. A reader of the summary alone gets the unscaled norm. Item 4 already has the exact identity.
proposed_correction: Say that the period is degλ‖W‖₂².

title: Specify how W is integrated over the unipotent quotient
reason: The vector W can change by the character ψ under a change of coset representative. Its norm descends to the quotient. Lean integrates W on G₁ with besselQuotMeasure, a cutoff-weighted Haar measure on G₁ that computes quotient integrals.
proposed_correction: Define μ on G₁ as besselQuotMeasure, or state that W is an integrable equivariant section and its norm is integrable on the quotient.

title: Correct the two library names for the decay estimates
reason: Both coefficient decay and the covering inequality live under New.DiscreteSeries. The generic coefficient result allows c ≤ h and is specialized at c = j + 9r². The covering theorem at TotalMass.lean line 466 takes a right-invariant measure finite on compact sets and c > 8r². The chosen Haar measure and exponent satisfy these conditions.
proposed_correction: Cite New.DiscreteSeries.norm_dsCoeff_le_pow and New.DiscreteSeries.lintegral_decay_le. Keep New.isIdempotentKernel_dsCoeffInFrame as written.

title: The period group is a semidirect product
reason: The summary writes R = U × H as a group. The product is a coordinate description of the underlying space. In the group law H acts on U by conjugation, as the proof on this page shows.
proposed_correction: Write R = U ⋊ H in the summary and reserve U × H for the Haar coordinates.

title: Specify the unipotent Haar normalization
reason: The page names the compact Haar measure but only calls du a Haar measure. The value of the displayed Bessel average scales with du. Lean fixes besselHaar by pushing forward the product of Lebesgue measure on the upper entries and besselHaar₀.
proposed_correction: Identify du as New.Shape.besselHaar and dh as Haar probability, so the average has its source normalization.

title: Point the sign-frame reference to its declared namespace
reason: The placeholder names New.SignFrame. The class that supplies the matrix taking the Hermitian form to the sign diagonal is New.DiscreteSeries.SignFrame.
proposed_correction: Replace the target with New.DiscreteSeries.SignFrame.

title: Point the sign-frame reference to its declaring namespace
reason: The link expects New.SignFrame. New.DiscreteSeries.UnitarySignFrame extends New.DiscreteSeries.SignFrame, the class whose Gram identity supplies the conjugation into U(ε).
proposed_correction: Change the placeholder to New.DiscreteSeries.SignFrame.

title: Define the dimension in the cutoff error exponent
reason: The first use of r is the condition r ≥ 100. Its cube sets the decay rate. Lean takes r to be the size of the matrices in G₁, while the preceding text defines only n.
proposed_correction: Introduce r = 2ϱ + |κ| + 1 as the matrix size and f as a positive integer before stating the estimate.

title: State that rep is a continuous unitary representation
reason: The theorem introduces a continuous map from U(κ) to U(I). The construction also needs its homomorphism property, which appears in the Lean type →* and gives the transformation law for the normalized Bessel function. The linked definition of the average uses this structure.
